A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we provide a new framework for learning from incomplete data and establish the relationships between the upper-best approximate learning from incomplete data, the upper-best learning from positive data and some important notions of quasi-order and topology theory.
we have established some fundamental theorems on approximate identifiability which are quite different from the results in the conventional PAC model.
the upper-best approximations of concepts in the limit from complete data are always identifiable in the limit, but the upper-best approximated concepts in the limit may not always be identifiable.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the closure properties of concept classes play a crucial role for the approximate learning in the limit.

the closure property is a necessary and sufficient condition for the upper-best approximate learnability in the limit from complete data and a sufficient condition for the lower-best approximate learnability from positive data, respectively.
, in the framework of approximate learning, the concept class is a more natural notion than hypothesis space.
